intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: functional requirement — Behaviour a system must provide.
non-functional requirement — Quality or constraint on system operation.
acceptance criterion — Condition showing requirement has been met.
trade-off — Choice balancing competing advantages and costs.

blocks.title: Analyse the brief
blocks.text: Separate stakeholder requirements, constraints, risk and available resources.

blocks.title: Choose a lifecycle
blocks.text: Justify one method against credible alternatives with evidence.

blocks.title: Trace a core algorithm
blocks.text: Write and test one key decision procedure that fits the brief.

blocks.title: Worked example · Model answer
blocks.text: Use iterative development for changing fare rules with documented acceptance milestones for launch. Fare algorithm: collect zones and passenger category, select valid tariff, compute fare, reject invalid input and test boundary zones. Check: link each claim to the scenario and use precise OCR terminology.

blocks.title: Shared worked answer
blocks.text: RAD or agile prototypes gather pupil feedback quickly; keep data security and payment assurance as formal checks. Algorithm checks available stock, valid quantity and eligibility before confirming order.
